clue.text: Feel sorry for soldiers cooped up

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers
pent, as in pent-up, means shut in or confined

explanation.surface: Someone sympathises with troops stuck in their barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooped up' looks like it describes the soldiers, but it is the second piece, PENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to show remorse for a wrong one has done.

clue.text: Line of sight?

parts.note: reads as a view across a landscape, but means the fine crossed lines in a gunsight or telescope eyepiece

explanation.walkthrough: The lines are literal: the hairlines etched in an optical sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticle is the grid of fine crosshairs in the eyepiece of a sighting instrument.

clue.text: What the doctor may make of poor signs

indicators.note: to make something of the letters is to build a new word out of them, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written into the anagram

explanation.surface: A doctor interprets weak symptoms in a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' looks like the anagram signal for 'signs', but it is fodder too: POOR and SIGNS together are rearranged, signalled by 'make of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast of how an illness will run is what a physician gives after examining the patient.

clue.text: It ensures you won't be spotted at mealtimes

definitions.text: It ensures you won't be spotted at mealtimes

parts.words: It ensures you won't be spotted at mealtimes
parts.note: spotted suggests being seen, but means stained with food splashes

explanation.definitionFit: A cloth or paper square tucked in or laid on the lap keeps food stains off clothes.

clue.text: Masefield's main complaint

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a complaint is an illness, such as a fever

explanation.walkthrough: John Masefield's best-known poem is Sea Fever ('I must go down to the seas again'); 'main complaint' reads as chief grumble but splits into sea plus illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea Fever is the famous poem written by John Masefield, so it is Masefield's work.

clue.text: They can't fly me up to the land of the free

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word me is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a phrase from the US national anthem for America

explanation.surface: Flightless creatures ask to be flown to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They can't fly' reads as a refusal to travel by plane; it is the flightless birds. The anthem's 'land of the free' is America.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless birds from Australia.

clue.text: Squanders food

explanation.definitionFit: To fritter money is to waste it bit by bit; fritters are also pieces of food fried in batter.

clue.text: Lacking a roadway site

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: an avenue is a broad street or roadway

explanation.surface: A place with no road access.
explanation.walkthrough: AVENUE without A gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place or location where an event is held.

clue.text: Jackets for hippies

explanation.definitionFit: Reefers are short double-breasted sailors' coats, and also cannabis cigarettes, associated with the hippie culture of the 1960s.

clue.text: They may advance or stop if ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers who either march forward or halt when commanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' suggests a military command, but it signals the rearranging of OR STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers move forward against an enemy in an attack.

clue.text: People at play

parts.note: suggests people enjoying games, but means the people watching a theatre play

explanation.definitionFit: Those who watch a theatrical performance are its spectators.

clue.text: Brilliant spectacle opening up over Etna, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gap is an opening

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A dazzling sight as the Sicilian volcano erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening up' looks like an eruption, but gives GAP turned upwards (PAG); 'perhaps' rearranges ETNA as EANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand, colourful public show or procession.

clue.text: There's some humanity in him, no doubt

definitions.text: There's some humanity in him, no doubt

parts.words: There's some humanity in him, no doubt
parts.note: humanity suggests kindness, but means pieces of human beings eaten and lying in his stomach

explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats human flesh literally has bits of people inside.

clue.text: Female embraced by one female deity or another

indicators.note: embraced means held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A woman hugged by one goddess or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one female deity or another' reads as one phrase; it splits, with 'another' (goddess) as the definition. Ate is a lesser-known Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom, a second goddess after Ate.

clue.text: A prize for waste

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: Someone wins an award for squandering.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is to waste away, as an unused muscle does.

clue.text: The right side of the map

definitions.text: The right side of the map

parts.words: The right side of the map
parts.note: suggests the correct side, but means the side on the right as a map is normally drawn

explanation.definitionFit: Maps are drawn with north at the top, so the compass point on the right-hand edge is this.

clue.text: Nine crates of mixed fruit

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled, so the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed fruit' reads as one phrase, but 'mixed' signals the rearranging of NINE and CRATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectarines are smooth-skinned peaches.

clue.text: At noon it's changing character, or characters

indicators.note: a thing changing its character takes a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: At midday something alters its nature.
explanation.walkthrough: AT NOON and IT'S rearranged give the answer; 'or' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Notations are systems of written symbols, such as musical or chemical signs.

clue.text: Partition between pigs and birds

indicators.note: between puts the partition inside, splitting the pig word in two

parts.note: sows are female pigs
a wall is a dividing partition

explanation.surface: A divider separating pigs from birds on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between pigs and birds' looks like a fence between two groups of animals; only 'birds' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallows are small, fork-tailed migratory birds.

clue.text: Light that goes up and down

definitions.text: Light that goes up and down

parts.words: Light that goes up and down
parts.note: light suggests a lamp, but here means a window, whose panes slide vertically

explanation.definitionFit: A window made of panes in frames that slide vertically in grooves is opened by raising or lowering it.

clue.text: Pull out in time

explanation.definitionFit: To stretch is to pull something longer; a stretch is also a period of time, especially a prison sentence.

clue.text: A bit of a fag, perhaps

definitions.text: A bit of a fag, perhaps

parts.words: A bit of a fag, perhaps
parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a fag is a cigarette; the clue also hints at a chore, another British sense of fag.
explanation.definitionFit: The short remnant of a smoked cigarette is its end or butt.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts

explanation.definitionFit: Bananas are a tropical fruit; going bananas is slang for being crazy, which is also what nuts means.

clue.text: The cad is out to break the engagement

indicators.note: out means displaced, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scoundrel leaves to call off a planned marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' suggests marriage but means connection: to separate or disengage. 'is out' rearranges THE CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach is to unfasten or disconnect, ending the joining of two parts.

clue.text: Actually it's about a friend

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.definitionFit: Really means in fact or in truth.

clue.text: Sliding calculator

explanation.definitionFit: An adder is a snake, which moves by gliding along the ground; it is also a device or circuit that adds numbers.

clue.text: Give warning to number after earthquake

indicators.note: after places the number piece second, behind the rearranged letters
to quake is to shake, so the letters of the preceding word are shaken into a new order

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: An authority alerts people after a tremor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earthquake' looks like one word, but splits: 'quake' rearranges 'earth' as THREA, and 'after' puts the number behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten is to warn of harm to come.

clue.text: Endless danger for a fairy

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: peril is danger

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale creature faces constant threat.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or sprite of Persian legend.

clue.text: Swimmers who will leap ahead when detailed

definitions.text: Swimmers who will leap ahead when detailed

parts.words: Swimmers who will leap ahead when detailed
parts.note: detailed suggests given particulars, but means having lost their tails, when these swimmers become frogs and jump

explanation.definitionFit: Young frogs swim with tails, which they lose as they grow into leaping adults.

clue.text: Dark red strand

explanation.definitionFit: Maroon is a deep brownish-crimson colour; to maroon is to strand someone, as on a desert island.

clue.text: Suffering which might make a crew mutiny?

definitions.text: which might make a crew mutiny?

explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is severe trouble; split as hard ship, it is a harsh vessel that might drive sailors to revolt.

clue.text: Primate rushes around

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monkey dashes all over the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus is a macaque monkey of South Asia.
